sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellant - respondent No.1 submits that the Tribunal erred in awarding 50% of sum of Rs.2,06,000/- towards the compensation along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum so far as APSRTC is concerned as against the claim of Rs.5,00,000/- in case of injuries under Section 166 of the MV Act, has committed irregularity in holding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-28-Y-5592 without there being any acceptable evidence BRMR,J on record, failed to frame an issue whether the claim against APSRTC is liable to be dismissed as the crime vehicle was hired by the APSRTC and ought to have appreciated the fact that the injured was on foot board negligently in the bus-bay of Bowenpally bus stop which is restricted to anyone to stand in the bus-bay and caused accident without giving way to the bus.

As per Ex.A4 - C.C of charge sheet, at the time of accident the injured was walking on the road as such there is no contradictions between the version of the charge sheet and the claim petition with regard to the manner in which the accident has taken place.
The Tribunal erred in taking the income of the injured at Rs.500/- per day.
Ex.A9 - disability certificate is issued by PW3.
The learned Tribunal ought to have appreciated the fact that the insurance company shall be solely and exclusively liable to pay the compensation arising out of third party claims.

Counsel to substantiate his contention has relied on the decisions in the cases of (i) The National Insurance Company Limited, Hyderabad Vs. C.H.Balram and others 1 and (ii)
Smt.K.Jayasree and others Vs. K.Shankara Reddy and others 2 and prayed to allow the appeal.

sentences.text: Now the point for consideration is: Whether the appellant - respondent No.1 is liable to be indemnified by respondent No.3.

10. The learned Tribunal while answering issue No.1, arrived at a conclusion that the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW1 is sufficient to come to a conclusion that the driver of bus bearing No.AP-28-Y-5592 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and BRMR,J dashed PW1 though he was walking cautiously on the road and held that driver of the crime vehicle is at fault.
11.

Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the learned Tribunal has taken the income of respondent No.1 - petitioner at Rs.500/- per day, he lost 76 days due to the injuries and the said period has to be treated as loss of earning and arrived at Rs.38,000/- (500 x 76).
12. PW3-Dr.B.Sugunakar Reddy deposed that respondent No.1 - petitioner has sustained disability at 10%.

The Tribunal has taken the income of the respondent No.1 - petitioner at Rs.15,000/- per month, deducted 1/3rd towards his personal expenses and arrived at Rs.10,000/- per month [15,000 - (1/3rd of 15,000)], arrived annual income at Rs.1,20,000/-, applied multiplier '14' as he falls in the age group of 40-45 as per Smt. Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another 3 and arrived at Rs.16,80,000/-, assessed disability at 10% and arrived loss of income due to disability at Rs.1,68,000/- (16,80,000 x 10%).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the learned Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.38,000/- towards loss of earning.
Total compensation comes to Rs.2,06,000/- and awarded interest at the (2009) 6 SCC 121 BRMR,J rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till deposit.

Further learned Tribunal held that it is appropriate to directed respondent Nos.1 and 3 to pay the compensation in the ratio of 50 : 50.
13.1

In CH.Balram1 the High Court observed at page No.7 which reads as under:
'There is no dispute with regard to the principles laid down in Palitana Sugar Mills Pvt. Ltd and another Vs. Smt. Vilasiniben Ramachandran and others's case - (AIR 2007 SC 1701).

entities.text: Palitana Sugar Mills Pvt. Ltd and another Vs. Smt. Vilasiniben Ramachandran and others's case - (AIR 2007 SC 1701)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But it is also settled legal position that each case has to be decided on its own facts and circumstances.
In the instant case, admittedly, the vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company and the policy is subsisting as on the date of accident.
It is also not in dispute that the vehicle has been hired by APSRTC.
It is not the contention of the learned counsel for the review petitioner that there is a condition in the policy that the vehicle should not be hired with anyone.

The facts of the case in Purnya Kala Devi Vs. State of Assam and another - (2014 (4) Scale 586)
appears to be some what different.

entities.text: Purnya Kala Devi Vs. State of Assam and another - (2014 (4) Scale 586)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case, the vehicle was not insured.
Admittedly, it was under the requisition of the State Government at the relevant time.
In the light of the definition of the word 'owner', it was respondent-State has to be treated the owner of the vehicle.

Even if respondent-APSRTC is treated as owner of the vehicle, it does not absolve the Insurance Company from its liability since the Insurance Company had undertaken to indemnify the liability of the owner.
Thus, be it the registered owner or the hirer, both are covered under the definition of word 'owner' under Section 2(30) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Therefore, even after holding that APSRTC is deemed owner and is also liable to pay compensation, the Apsrtc, Rep By Is M.D., Hyderabad vs M Ramesh Rao, Secunderabad And 2 Others on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186214055/
3 Insurance Company has to indemnify the APSRTC."

entities.text: Apsrtc, Rep By Is M.D., Hyderabad vs M Ramesh Rao, Secunderabad And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: BRMR,J 13.2

In Smt.K.Jayasree2, the High Court observed at paragraph No.12(c),
which reads as under:
"It may be noted that when the ratio of the above decision is applied to the instant case, the APSRTC who was the hirer at the time of accident may at best be regarded as owner of the vehicle.
However by that count alone, the liability of insurance company will not be ceased, since it took the risk of third parties through Ex.B.1-policy.

The Insurance Company shall indemnify the liability of both the registered owner i.e, R.1 in the O.P and also the deemed owner i.e, APSRTC (hirer) /
R.3 and R.4 in the O.P.

This point is answered accordingly."
14.
Respondent No.3 has filed counter in the main O.P., and contended that the policy number issued to the crime vehicle as mentioned in the petition is not tallying with the records.
Respondent No.3 has not adduced any evidence, not placed any record to show that the policy which is issued to the claim petitioner is not tallying with the records of respondent No.3.
Hence the contention of the learned counsel for respondent No.3 is negatived.
15. In view of the decisions in CH.Balram1 and Smt.K.Jayasree2, respondent No.3 - insurance company should indemnify APSRTC and pay the entire amount.
Learned counsel for the appellant - respondent No.1 submits that they have deposited amount before the learned Tribunal while obtaining stay in MACMA.MP.No.4685 of 2015, BRMR,J dated 08.10.2015.
The appellant - respondent No.1 can recover the deposited amount from the respondent No.3 - insurance company.
Insurance company shall be liable to pay the entire awarded amount to respondent No.1 - petitioner less the amount already paid if any.
16. With the above observation, MACMA.No.622 of 2016 is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Interim orders if any shall stand vacated, miscellaneous application/s pending if any shall stand closed.
